job.title: Group Manager Infrastructure Services
job.description:
City of Parramatta sits at the centre of Sydney’s Central City, a metropolitan council of significant scale and profile serving a community of 286,000. Its infrastructure services keep that city functioning: the roads, drainage, parks, fleet and facilities that residents rely on every day. Leading them is one of the most substantial operational appointments in New South Wales local government.

The Group Manager Infrastructure Services leads this portfolio at both ends: setting strategy and budget at the executive table and commanding the confidence of the operational workforce who deliver the work on the ground. It is a role that rewards genuine operational credibility as much as strategic capability.

The Role
Reporting to the Executive Director City Services and Projects, the Group Manager Infrastructure Services leads the operational heart of Council. The portfolio spans the maintenance of roads, footpaths, drainage, parks and open space, facilities, fleet and light and heavy plant, and depot and store operations, delivered through a multidisciplinary team of professionals, each section led by a Service Manager. Your direct reports lead a workforce of around 140 people.

The role carries whole-of-life accountability for Council’s fleet and plant assets, strategic direction and budget oversight for the business unit, and the position of Local Emergency Management Officer (LEMO), a function that grows more consequential each year as communities expect more of their council in preparedness and response.

This is a role for an experienced operational leader who understands that service delivery in a high-profile metropolitan environment is as much about judgement, stakeholder navigation and organisational influence as it is about technical competence.

About You
You are a proven leader of outdoor workforces and multidisciplinary teams. You bring depth in asset maintenance and operational service delivery, a clear grasp of the legislative environment, and the commercial discipline to manage significant budgets with rigour. Local government experience is preferred, though we welcome operational leaders from state government or other comparable environments who can demonstrate the same command of service delivery at scale.

Just as important is how you lead. You earn credibility rather than assert it. You are as comfortable providing authoritative advice to an Executive Team and Councillors as you are on the ground with the crews, genuinely at ease talking shop with an outdoor workforce and trusted by them for it. You move between those worlds with authenticity, and you bring alignment to capable teams, drawing structured and operationally minded people toward a common standard. You understand that embedded safety culture, asset sustainability and high-performing teams are not competing priorities but the product of the same disciplined, people-first leadership.

A degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Land Management/ Parks, Business Management or a related discipline, is required combined with relevant management and leadership experience

Why This Role
Parramatta offers something few councils can. This is a genuinely significant operational remit, an executive environment that takes infrastructure seriously, and the platform of one of Australia’s most recognisable local government brands at the centre of a city being reshaped. For the right operational leader, this is a defining appointment.

Security Operations and Engineering

  • Experience providing leadership and governance oversight for security and protective security functions within a complex operational environment.
  • Proven ability to balance strategic leadership with operational accountability, delivering high-quality services while managing risk, compliance, budgets and organisational priorities.
  • Strong track record in leading multidisciplinary teams, fostering an inclusive and high-performance culture, and developing capability to achieve both individual and organisational objectives.
  • Ability to identify, assess and respond to complex challenges, risks and interdependencies, applying sound judgement to deliver sustainable and effective business outcomes.
  • Extensive stakeholder engagement and relationship management experience, with the ability to build trust, influence decision-making and collaborate effectively with executives, regulators, service providers, and diverse business groups.
  • Demonstrated experience managing significant outsourced service arrangements and vendor partnerships, ensuring value for money, contractual compliance, service excellence and continuous improvement.
  • Proven ability to lead organisational change, drive innovation and implement improvement initiatives that enhance service delivery, operational efficiency and workplace outcomes.
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications in Engineering, Asset Management, Sustainability, Facilities Management, Business, Security Management or a related discipline.
  • Professional certifications or memberships relevant to asset management, engineering, sustainability, facilities management, security, project management or leadership.

job.title: Transport Planning Lead
job.description:
Senior Investment Planning Lead | Transport & Infrastructure | Queensland
 
Our client is a highly regarded engineering consultancy with a strong track record of delivering complex transport infrastructure studies for Transport and Main Roads (TMR) across Queensland. They are seeking a senior leader to drive the winning and delivery of investment planning engagements, with a clear pathway to grow a high-performing team in this space.
 
The Opportunity
This is a genuine leadership role for someone who has built their career in TMR investment planning and is ready to take ownership of both business development and project delivery. You will lead the pursuit and delivery of Options Analysis, Business Case, Preliminary Evaluation and Business Case studies under TMR's OnQ and Project Assurance Framework (PAF) processes, working across a portfolio that ranges from focused $200k studies through to complex, multi-stage engagements valued at $10m or more.

What makes this opportunity particularly compelling is the long-term revenue potential these engagements carry. Strong performance at the Options Analysis stage routinely leads to ongoing appointments through Business Case and into Detailed Design, meaning the work you win and deliver today builds a substantial pipeline for tomorrow.
 
What You Will Be Doing
  • Leading the preparation of tenders and proposals for TMR investment planning opportunities, including methodology development, resource planning and pricing
  • Managing the delivery of OnQ (OA and BC) and PAF (PE and BC) engagements as Study Manager or Project Manager
  • Building and maintaining trusted relationships with TMR project managers and stakeholders across districts and regions
  • Contributing to the strategic growth of the practice
 
What You Will Bring
You are likely 15 to 20 years into your career, with 3 to 5 years of experience leading investment planning studies for TMR in a study or project manager capacity. You have a solid and focused career history in this discipline, a genuine network of TMR contacts, and a track record of successful proposals and well-delivered engagements. RPEQ is required for engineers.

A background in traffic engineering or traffic modelling, TMR Road Safety Auditor accreditation, and established relationships with SEQ councils would all be well regarded.
 
Why Consider This Role?
This is a rare opportunity to step into a role with real influence, working with a consultancy that has the runs on the board, an established client in TMR, and a genuine appetite to grow. If you have been looking for a platform to lead rather than contribute, this is worth a conversation.
 
All enquiries are treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Chief Financial Officer
job.description:
The numbers have never mattered more.
AlburyCity is one of regional Australia's most significant urban centres, the commercial, cultural and service heart of a cross-border community on the Murray River. It is a growing city, and growth of this scale places real demands on an organisation's finances: major infrastructure to fund, rising cost pressures to manage, and a community rightly focused on value and long-term sustainability.

Council is currently engaging its community on a potential Special Rate Variation, a conversation about how AlburyCity funds the services and infrastructure the city will need for decades to come. It is against this backdrop that Council has created a new executive role: a Chief Financial Officer to lead its financial strategy at a genuinely pivotal moment.

The Opportunity
Reporting to the Deputy CEO, Business, Growth and Community, and sitting on the Executive Leadership Group, the Chief Financial Officer is AlburyCity's principal financial advisor, Responsible Accounting Officer and Responsible Reporting Officer under the Local Government Act 1993.
This is a role of genuine influence. You will lead the Finance, Procurement and Project Management Office functions, and oversee the disciplines that keep the organisation sustainable: long-term financial planning, budgeting and modelling, treasury, rating and revenue, internal controls, and the governance of a substantial capital works program.
As a newly created position, it carries a clear mandate: to embed evidence-based financial decision-making across the organisation, to strengthen the link between affordability and ambition, and to ensure that every strategic choice Council makes is grounded in sound numbers. This is stewardship with purpose, building the financial capability of the whole organisation so that good decisions become the norm.

What You Will Lead
  • Council's financial sustainability and fiscal management agenda, including long-term financial planning, budgeting, financial modelling and the delivery of efficiencies and cost containment
  • Strategic oversight of financial operations: rating, revenue, debt, treasury, statutory and management reporting, procurement and contract management
  • Governance of the capital works program through the Project Management Office, ensuring prioritisation, affordability, funding alignment and delivery
  • The Finance, Procurement and PMO teams, through three Team Leaders, fostering a high-performing, accountable and continuously improving culture

What You Will Bring
You are an accomplished senior finance leader with deep expertise in corporate financial management: long-term planning, budgeting, treasury, modelling and financial sustainability. You hold tertiary qualifications in Finance, Business, Management or a related field. Essential to the role, you hold a current CA or CPA qualification.
You combine technical authority with the judgement to operate in a politically sensitive environment, balancing competing priorities while holding the confidence of Councillors, executive colleagues and the community. You interpret legislation with confidence, you translate complex financial matters into clear advice, and you lead people exceptionally well. This is a role where people leadership is central. You will build and rebuild a capable, cohesive finance function, leading teams through change and shaping a culture of accountability, engagement and continuous improvement.
A sound understanding of NSW Local Government legislation, Australian Accounting Standards and Integrated Planning and Reporting obligations will see you make an early impact. Just as importantly, you bring the integrity and steadiness this moment asks of the role.
Why AlburyCity
Few finance roles offer this combination: a growing regional city, a genuinely strategic mandate, a new position you can shape, and a lifestyle that many in the sector aspire to. AlburyCity offers the scale and complexity of a significant urban council with the connection and liveability of regional NSW

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
Lead a shire on the cusp of a generational transformation.
Moree Plains sits at the heart of Northwest NSW, at the junction of the Newell, Gwydir and Carnarvon Highways. Its black soil plains and secure water grow more than a billion dollars of agricultural produce each year, in cotton, grain, oilseeds, livestock and oranges. It is one of the most productive agricultural economies in the country, and it is entering its most exciting chapter yet.

The Moree Special Activation Precinct, a 4,716-hectare industry precinct south of the town centre, is backed by the NSW Government to drive population growth and attract new industry across high-value horticulture, agrifood processing, freight and logistics, and renewable energy over the coming decades. It is the most significant economic opportunity in the shire's history.
The region’s producers are renowned for innovation, with Australia’s first Green Hydrogen project and other sustainable initiatives ensuring the continued growth of the ag sector. Harnessing that momentum, while keeping Council financially sustainable and delivering for existing ratepayers, is the defining leadership opportunity of this role.

The Opportunity
As General Manager, you hold ultimate responsibility for the management and direction of all Council operations. You are the single point of connection between the elected Council and the organisation, translating the Community Strategic Plan into services the community can see and rely on, and giving the Mayor and Councillors the strategic advice and honest counsel that good decisions depend on.

This is a whole-of-organisation leadership role at a genuine inflection point. You will lead the executive team, own the long-term financial and asset management plans that keep the shire sustainable, and leverage external opportunities so that the community and local economy capture the benefit. It is a role for a leader who wants their work to matter, in a place where the decisions made over the next few years will shape the shire for the next forty.
The Person
You are an accomplished senior executive with a proven record of transforming organisational culture and building high-performing teams. You are a strategic operator who can lead a discerning review of an organisation's plans and budgets, safeguard the effective use of public funds, and hold the line on financial sustainability while still setting ambitious, achievable goals.

You bring genuine experience delivering major projects to a high standard and embedding best-practice project management, and you understand and can lead best-practice governance. You lead with energy and presence, you drive productivity, and you build pride in serving the community. You are a skilled engager of communities and stakeholders, with the cultural competence and commitment to work genuinely and effectively with Aboriginal communities. Experience in a role of comparable size and scope is preferred, and tertiary qualifications in business, management or a related discipline are well regarded.

Why Moree Plains
Moree Plains offers a relaxed, connected regional lifestyle, the artesian hot springs, the rivers of the Gwydir Valley, space and affordability that the cities cannot match, and a community that is ambitious about its future. This is a place at a turning point, and a rare chance to lead an organisation through the change that will define it. Few local government roles in NSW offer this combination of statutory leadership, genuine transformation, and the ability to leave a lasting mark on a community.

job.title: Head of Capital Transactions

A rare opportunity to help lead the next phase of growth for one of Melbourne's most respected independent real estate investment groups – Forza Capital. This newly created role has been established to support a clearly defined growth plan, working alongside the Directors and Head of Capital, together with a high-performing Melbourne-based team. Opportunities of this calibre, seniority, founder-facing and newly created, rarely present themselves in the Melbourne market.
ABOUT FORZA CAPITAL
Forza Capital is an independently owned Australian real estate investment group with a sixteen-year track record of disciplined, high-conviction investing. Since inception, the business has executed 24 real estate investments totalling $1.55 billion in transactional activity, delivering an average net IRR of 19.7 per cent (after fees) across completed funds and 15 exits to date.
Operating across the office, industrial and retail sectors in Melbourne and Sydney, Forza Capital describes itself as “investors, not fund managers”: a business built on patient capital, hands-on asset management and long-term relationships rather than growth for its own sake. The Directors remain closely involved in every transaction, and this role has been created to support the next stage of the business's expansion.

Reporting to, and working directly alongside the Directors, the Head of Capital Transactions will take a lead role in originating, structuring and executing real estate transactions across the group's investment mandates. You will be a highly visible, trusted advisor at the centre of the business, with genuine influence over strategy, deal selection and outcomes, while working closely with a talented and collaborative Melbourne team.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead origination, structuring and execution of real estate acquisitions and divestments across office, industrial and retail assets
  • Partner directly with the senior leadership to shape and deliver the business's growth strategy
  • Manage transaction due diligence, negotiations and settlement processes, working alongside legal, finance and asset management teams
  • Build and maintain relationships with vendors, selling agents, capital partners and other market participants
  • Prepare investment papers, financial models and board-level recommendations
  • Mentor and support members of the capital transactions team

  • Ability to operate autonomously and take ownership of outcomes.

  • High level of professionalism, accountability, and integrity.

Experience working within a vertically integrated development and construction business will be highly regarded.

Benefits
